source_statement: Exact-BSD (Oct-7-2026), build/sections/03-models.tex:557-566, Lemma [Division from high characters] \label{models:series-division}: 'Let O be one of these complete integer DVRs and let L,B in O[[t,u]]. Suppose L != 0 (mod (varpi,t)), where varpi is a uniformizer. If, for every sufficiently high finite p-power character theta of 1+t, the specialization B(theta,u) is divisible by L(theta,u) after inversion of p, then L divides B integrally. The assertion applies simultaneously to finite products of such divisors and after the fixed constant extensions above.' Here 'these DVRs' are W(F_p-bar), V* = W(prod_U F_p-bar) and fixed finite ramified extensions (03-models.tex:544-549); 'bounded series' = coefficients in O or in Frac(O) with one common denominator (540-542); t is the genuine (cyclotomic over Q / anticyclotomic over K) variable and u the tame variables (04-vertical.tex:17-24, 156). Proof (568-591): group-power coordinate change 1+u_j=(1+x)^{n_j} makes L distinguished in one tame variable; Weierstrass-divide B by the monic polynomial; at each high theta the polynomial stays distinguished of the same degree and the quotient module is p-torsion-free, so the integral remainder vanishes at theta; its bounded coefficients vanish at infinitely many characters hence are zero by one-variable Weierstrass preparation. Closing line 588-590: 'It is the proof of [Lemma 3.10]{B}, with p in place of two', where [B] = the companion AI manuscript 'The two-primary BSD formula in Selmer corank at most one' (references.tex:157-162), whose version is 03-foundations.tex:372-377, lemma lem:foundations-series (a one-paragraph sketch). Use sites: 06-pair.tex:1048-1083 (Cor. pair:integral-quotient, U_w=B_w/L_w integral and p-free) fed by eq:source-1(b) = Prop. vertical:tests 04-vertical.tex:173-183 ('L_w, L'_w != 0 mod (p,t) for both w|p' after adjoining tame variables), Prop. pair:finite-divisibility 06-pair.tex:653-663 (divisibility at high theta, from CM points over an auxiliary K with E/K of rank one, 04-vertical.tex:13-16) and Prop. pair:vertical-primitivity eq:source-14 06-pair.tex:406-413 (p does not divide B_w); and 09-unit.tex:106-125 (Lemma unit:association, mutual divisibility of U_w and U_wbar). Grade: IMPORTED_PREPRINT (unrefereed, AI-generated, no Lean for family 002). My own desk check of the lemma's argument: sound as commutative algebra (distinguished polynomial stays distinguished at theta because zeta-1 lies in the maximal ideal; O[zeta][[u']][u_1]/(P(theta)) is free of finite rank hence p-torsion-free; a series in O[[u']][[t]] vanishing at infinitely many zeta-1 is zero coefficientwise); V* is a DVR because an ultraproduct of fields is a field. It is standard Weierstrass-preparation material, not a theorem the lab needs to import.
what_it_would_need: To be an input to any seed obligation the lemma needs its three hypotheses supplied for a seed object; each is a separate missing theorem and none is supplied by the manuscript for rank two. (a) Residual concentration for a rank-two center: a bounded two-variable family (cyclotomic t plus tame u_1..u_m) whose algebraic determinant L satisfies L != 0 mod (p,t). For the seed at p >= 5 the two saturated points inject independently into the residual strict Selmer space at t=0 (tors = Z/2), so the central residual nullity is >= 2 and L(0,u) == 0 mod p until tame deformations kill a two-dimensional space. The manuscript proves this only via Prop. vertical:tests eq:source-1(b) (04-vertical.tex:173-183), whose parity/acyclicity step vertical:parity (252-267) uses 'one compact Selmer line from points' whose localization at a p-place is nonzero; for the seed the localization of the point plane into one local Kummer line has a kernel, so the step must be replaced by a rank-two residual-concentration theorem: two tame directions (moving primes with variables) whose first-order cup tests separate both residual point classes simultaneously -- precisely the missing theorem. (b) Divisibility at high characters (the analogue of Prop. pair:finite-divisibility, 06-pair.tex:653-663): for E over Q this is an integral two-variable Kato/IMC-type statement 'L_p(theta) | det Sel(theta) after inverting p' at high cyclotomic characters, i.e. a tame-deformed cyclotomic main-conjecture divisibility; available published inputs are per prime (Kato one direction; Skinner-Urban at good ordinary p with irreducibility/ramification hypotheses; none at the supersingular, additive 4547, or multiplicative 2243/5843 seed primes in this tame-deformed form). The manuscript's own version is built from CM points over an auxiliary imaginary quadratic K with E/K rank one and all primes dividing 2Np split (classical:auxiliary-fields, 02-classical.tex:115-137): no such K exists for the seed (rank E(K) >= 2 for every K), and the lab's K = Q(sqrt -7) has 3, 2243, 5843 inert. (c) Vertical primitivity p does not divide B (eq:source-14) for the seed's analytic/Kato element -- a strict-primitivity statement the lab has explicitly withdrawn as the required target ('Strict primitivity is sufficient but is no longer the required target', CURRENT_STATE.md). Even with (a)-(c), the output is integrality of the quotient U = B/L only; the lab's target m_p - w_p <= 1 is a bound on the central p-content of that quotient, which the lemma cannot give (Codex's countercontrol) and which the manuscript obtains separately via the horizontal-divisor exclusion of §8-9 (extraction:theta-implication, unit:simultaneous-jumps), whose arithmetic input is again the rank-one acyclicity. For the cofinite (FIN uniform) part the lemma is per-prime and silent. For 59, 487, 2243, 4547, 5843 it offers no computation. For ORDER9/Q36 nothing. For the plectic lemma TH at 5843 (nonvanishing of c_1(lambda_ell) at a multiplicative prime inert in K) nothing: the manuscript's K-side construction excludes nonsplit bad places from the support (04-vertical.tex:28-34) and assumes split 2Np. Cost reduction: none (pure algebra, no computation to replace).
obligation: None served. Nearest conceivable target: the per-prime integrality step inside the Kato-derivative route (delta_p != 0, m_p - w_p <= 1 => Sha[p^infty]=0 at good p >= 5 outside {19,59,487}), where it could replace an ad hoc 'specialize then divide' step once a tame-deformed two-variable Kato/determinant family with residual concentration exists for the rank-two center; it cannot supply the content bound m_p - w_p <= 1 itself. Not applicable to FIN-uniform, 59/487/2243/4547/5843, ORDER9, Q36, lemma TH at 5843, or cost reduction. K-A: using it would require assuming no conjecture, but every seed-side hypothesis is itself an unproved theorem. K-RANK2: the lemma has no rank hypothesis, but its only nontrivial input (eq:source-1(b)) is proved in the manuscript from the rank-one anchor. K-GRADE: IMPORTED_PREPRINT; the lemma is standard enough that the lab would state and prove it in work/ rather than cite the preprint.
new_observation: NEW-1: Codex's 'valid research possibility' of adding tame variables is not a new possibility; it is the manuscript's own design (04-vertical.tex:1-9) and its output is exactly Prop. vertical:tests eq:source-1(b) (04-vertical.tex:173-183). So the lemma's hypothesis L != 0 mod (p,t) is, in the manuscript, a theorem proved in §4 and the rank-one input enters there (vertical:parity 260-262), i.e. the division lemma and the rank-one anchor are not separable in the way the Codex summary suggests: the lemma is rank-free but empty without the rank-dependent concentration statement. NEW-2: The lab's G2-detecting auxiliaries (Frobenius -I, both points detected) are the natural candidates for the two tame directions a rank-two residual-concentration statement would need (both residual point classes must be separated by first-order cup tests, cf. 'first-order deformations separate every surviving residual Selmer class', 04-vertical.tex:7-8). This is a direction, not a result; it would have to be written and proved and is unrelated to the division lemma's content. NEW-3: The proof of models:series-division is deferred to the companion AI preprint [B] Lemma 3.10 = two-primary paper 03-foundations.tex:372-377 (lem:foundations-series), a one-paragraph sketch; the chain is preprint-to-preprint. I checked the argument independently: it is correct for any complete mixed-characteristic DVR (including V*, as an ultraproduct of fields is a field), so correctness is not the issue; the issue is that it is standard Weierstrass-preparation material and provides no arithmetic content. NEW-4: The manuscript's auxiliary-field hypothesis (02-classical.tex:125-126: every prime dividing 2Np splits in K, and E/K rank one, 04-vertical.tex:13-16) is unsatisfiable for the seed at any K, and the lab's K = Q(sqrt -7) has 3, 2243, 5843 inert -- so the manuscript's anticyclotomic divisibility input (pair:finite-divisibility) is structurally the split-prime Heegner setting, not the FG25 inert/level-raised setting of lemma TH; relevant to U3: nothing here at p|N inert in K. NEW-5: Oct-3 vs Oct-7: sections 03,04,06,09 byte-identical; the revision is citation-only (history.md:25). NEW-6: The lab file defining the z=Uy / d(U) object that Codex substituted (CURRENT_STATE.md links BSD_KATO_CONTENT_BOUND_CODEX_2026-10-07/VALUATION_TARGET.md) is not present in the lab_latest sync; the substitution test exists only inside Codex's note.
risks: Risk of over-reading: the lemma's rank-independence could be mistaken for applicability; its only substantive hypothesis is rank-one-derived in the source. Risk of over-grading: the lemma is correct but the manuscript as a whole is IMPORTED_PREPRINT with a preprint-to-preprint proof dependence ([B] Lemma 3.10); nothing in it is Lean-checked. Risk of mis-attribution: Codex's substitution object (z=Uy, d(U)) could not be checked against an independent lab record in this sync. Risk of wasted effort: pursuing 'add tame variables' as if new would replay the manuscript's §4 and hit the same rank-one acyclicity step Codex already located; any rank-two residual-concentration attempt is a new theorem, not a reuse. No assumption of Sha finiteness, rank-two Gross-Zagier, or the conclusion was used in this assessment (K-A); E^{-7} (corank 0) could in principle satisfy the manuscript's headline hypotheses but that is lead U1, not this lemma. FIN, ORDER9, Q36 unchanged.
